title: Build and measure a bounded concurrent system

objectives.text: Build a bounded single-producer/single-consumer typed-event pipeline with explicit FIFO/close/lifetime/correctness oracles, identifying untested failure and cancellation paths.

Capture raw monotonic event and run intervals with workload/build metadata, validate counts/order/checksum/capacity and report local distributions without claiming independent-arrival or production latency guarantees.

blocks.markdown: Build one local producer, one consumer and a capacity 8 fixed-storage ring of typed Events. Each of 5 fresh runs attempts values 1..128 in order; accepted values must be consumed exactly once in order, with count 128 and sum of squares 707264. There is no filtering, external input, network, account side effect or durable store. Closing rejects new items but drains accepted data. The same mutex guards all ring metadata/slots; each wait uses a state predicate. Shared result arrays are consumer-owned during work and main reads only after join.

Each Event stores a steady_clock timestamp immediately before the producer calls push. Its recorded response interval ends after the consumer pops it, checks ordering and adds its square to checksum, but BEFORE writing that event's timing sample and incrementing its completed counter. It includes producer push/admission waiting, queue waiting, notification/scheduling and that bounded processing, not pure service time. It excludes any intended independent arrival before the producer actually attempts push, and contains no application/network/durability time. Whole-run elapsed starts before consumer thread construction and ends after close/drain/join, excluding array/queue initialization and stdout formatting. Instrumentation/timer overhead remains included, not subtracted.

blocks.caption: C++20 -pthread; warning-clean baseline and separately labeled -O2 measurement build. Output varies: five RUN rows(run,elapsed_ns,count,checksum,ordered=1,high_water), each followed by 128 LAT rows(run,index,response_ns). Require count 128,checksum 707264,order 1,high_water 1..8 and nonnegative event intervals within that run. Nanoseconds are units, not promised precision. No exact expected timing stdout is asserted; variable measurement schema/work contract is checked. App C++ support unverified.

blocks.markdown: The inner close guard is declared after the consumer handle: it closes on ordinary producer scope exit before the handle's joining destructor. Queue/results outlive both. Thread-creation failure before the handle exists leaves no waiting consumer; normal close wakes a waiting consumer and drains items. As in the prior monitor, mutex/CV operations must succeed and the consumer must complete its bounded work. Ordinary stop requests do not automatically wake these CV waits. Worker exception supervision, stalled consumer, platform lock failure, cancellation deadlines, crash recovery and persistence are NOT implemented. Do not call this a production pipeline because its normal tests pass.

First compile with C++20/pthread and strict warnings; exact workload oracles must pass before interpreting timing. Test close-empty/full, FIFO with zero/duplicates, rejected pushes and wraparound in focused harnesses or prior queue concepts; distinguish those source/transition tests from this new EventRing revision's own checks. Run NDEBUG and memory/undefined-behavior safe-path diagnostics separately. They are not ThreadSanitizer or a full schedule proof. For each exact measured-source run validate five run records and 640 event records, counts, order, checksum and occupancy; keep raw values and source hash. Use an external timeout in the test harness to detect a hang, without presenting that timeout as a built-in cancellation guarantee.

blocks.caption: Synthetic report fixture only. Expected first line: {'n': 128, 'p99_ns': 100, 'max_ns': 900, 'completed': 128, 'high_water': 8}; second line work contract failed. At 128 observations nearest-rank p99 selects rank 127, so the single worst sample remains outside p99 but inside max. This function rejects a count 127 even with a plausible checksum. It validates stated fields, not native race freedom, input provenance or production SLOs.

blocks.markdown: A useful local report names exact source hash, toolchain/target/flags, OS/CPU metadata available, clock/units, run/event counts, queue/workload configuration and timing boundaries. Keep all 5 runs including their variation; no unannounced warmup discard. Provide each run elapsed time, completed throughput128*1e9/elapsed_ns, high-water mark and event nearest-rank p50/p95/p99/max, with raw observations. Do not average per-run p99 and call it pooled-event p99; report run scope explicitly. Record unknown scheduling/affinity/frequency/background load controls rather than assuming an isolated CPU. Sanitized timing rows remain separate from -O2 measurement rows.

Recorded local example, 2026-11-14 IST: GCC11.4.0, x86_64-linux-gnu, C++20 -pthread -O2 with strict warnings; Linux6.1.189+, reported Intel Xeon processor, reported 2 CPUs. Affinity/frequency/background load were not controlled or verified. All five fresh runs retained; each count 128, checksum 707264, FIFO order check passed. Integer ns are units, not accuracy. Source hash 5624805ed303cd832eea0b7833f4ae945d52ab4e43eb3f2ea022e35cbecebb8c.

These are actual observations of the exact authored source in one local environment, not synthetic examples. Raw RUN/LAT rows and all flags are retained in systems-measurement-verification-results.json and verification/measured-events-optimized-O2-raw.txt. Baseline/NDEBUG/ASan+UBSan diagnostic data are separate. No speed comparison, bottleneck profile or production tail/SLO inference is supported. Backpressured producer and small workload retain the limitations above.

Even a correct local result is one tiny synthetic in-process workload. The producer is paced by its previous push and can block on the ring; it is NOT an independent intended-arrival replay. Before-attempt timestamps include this push's waiting but not hypothetical unsent work during prior stalls. Five runs of 128 events cannot support a credible production p99.99 promise. This source records no CPU profile, off-CPU trace, hardware counter, per-stage service/admission split or comparison baseline. Thus it cannot establish a bottleneck, speedup, cache improvement or maximum latency. Those are distinct measurements/design work.

Independent transfer: change only event count and capacity in a clearly versioned local experiment, update exact count/sum-of-squares oracles and compare separately labeled raw reports. Keep close/drain/join and per-event observation count intact. To test independent arrivals, introduce a stated scheduled-arrival model and retain its original timestamps/lag/admission outcomes; do not merely rename attempt time. To claim cancellation or failure recovery, first design that protocol and coordinated tests. Produce a report that says what failed or remained unmeasured as clearly as what passed.

Sources: [steady_clock](https://en.cppreference.com/w/cpp/chrono/steady_clock.html), [predicate wait](https://eel.is/c++draft/thread.condition.condvar), [jthread](https://en.cppreference.com/w/cpp/thread/jthread.html), [percentile methods](https://www.itl.nist.gov/div898/handbook/prc/section2/prc262.htm) and [intended-arrival recording limitations](https://github.com/giltene/wrk2). The fixed ring/protocol/checksum/timing boundaries are own teaching contracts, not third-party benchmark results. Local captured measurements are evidence only for the recorded environment/build/run, never a market or production performance claim.

summary: A measured concurrent component needs exact correctness and lifetime contracts plus honest timing boundaries/raw observations. Separate normal-path safety tests, diagnostic builds and optimized local measurements. Small backpressured experiments do not prove production tail latency, cancellation or failure recovery.
